authorization_scope: Root relayed explicit user authorization to submit the three selected ready papers, with the recorded license, mixed origin, understanding-some provenance and attestations. This review authorizes no different paper, payload or declaration and makes no mathematical review claim.
method: Complete first-commit path and updated dispatch/journal source review, with static re-read of inherited preparation, fixed-origin request, exact upload/digest bindings and official cached OpenAPI commit response description. No credential or private receipt/PDF/log was opened; no client, request, compilation or scientific process was executed.
findings: The fixed official HTTPS origin, redirect refusal, disabled environment proxies, credential isolation and redaction, bounded responses and exact release-source/PDF checks remain intact. Commit accepts no arbitrary URL, public attachment, metadata override or manual preview-reviewed assertion.

All six mutating actions share one nonblocking private operation lock held for their entire execution. This closes the reviewed race between fresh commit validation and an upload or new preview. Both unresolved markers block new mutations; read-only status/artifact and local resolution paths remain available. The receipt journal has a separate append lock and atomic private replacement.

Commit rejects any previous commit attempt for the selected paper, unresolved preview or commit, and another locally recorded HTTP202 commit on the current UTC day. It performs no automatic retry. The remaining three-paper schedule requires the coordinator's later-day actions; this source creates no timer or background process.

The successful local content-review record must bind the current paper, draft, metadata, complete canonical file-manifest hash, reference-PDF hash, downloaded PDF hash, page count, bibliography, BibTeX and absence of final undefined references. Literal full-text equality or the separately reviewed explicit-today-only comparison is required. Artifact and terminal records must identify the exact same preview and opaque source digest; both downloaded PDF and log are rehashed.

Under the shared mutation lock, three fresh GETs revalidate exact remote metadata, the complete two-file upload set, each current immutable upload ID with its own exact-body PUT/completion receipts, exact sizes and the same ready source digest. Server-null content hashes are not represented as server-provided SHA evidence.

The live preview must still be the exact inspected identifier and digest, succeeded and current, with identical completion time and PDF size, PDF/log present, no error, and an allowed previewed gate without warning. No preview POST or TeX job is performed by the commit action, so its ordinary HTTP work does not acquire the scientific lane.

Before the one fixed-endpoint commit POST, an exclusive owner-only unresolved-commit marker is written and fsynced, and the request intent is journaled. Any error, uncertain result or non202 response leaves the hold for manual read-only reconciliation. Only HTTP202 permits a fsynced private per-paper submission receipt followed by marker removal. The successful response is described as asynchronous processing, not publication or screening success.

The original official OpenAPI describes this POST as reserving the permanent identifier and queuing source screening, with HTTP202 for asynchronous processing. Subsequent actual status and response-schema interpretation remain necessary before reporting publication or scheduling another day's deposit.
corrected_finding: The initial commit-only lock did not serialize concurrent upload or preview mutations. Final416f935c moves all mutating dispatch under the same operation lock and retains reconciliation reads outside it.
